author: evolve
description: Event-triggered companion to atlas-daily-digest. When a member of the configured Telegram group posts a URL, the bot fetches the article, summarizes it, classifies it into one of five buckets, files it in the same archive used by the daily digest, and reacts in-thread with a single bucket emoji so the member sees their contribution landed. Honors per-URL and per-user opt-out via slash commands.
objective: Make every URL a community member shares into a classified, summarized, opt-out-respecting archive entry — with visible feedback that the contribution was filed.
name: Atlas Article Capture

integrations.reason: Receives group messages + slash commands; posts reactions

identity.purpose: Turn community link-sharing into a durable, classified, opt-out-respecting archive — and give the member visible confirmation their contribution was filed. The archive is shared with atlas-daily-digest and atlas-weekly-recap, so a member-shared link can show up in tomorrow's digest or this week's recap.
scope_includes: When a group message contains one or more URLs: fetch each (respect robots.txt, 10s timeout, 5MB max), summarize, classify into one of the five Atlas buckets via the shared classifier
Write a Markdown archive entry to archive/{bucket}/ and append to archive/index.json
React in-thread on the source message with the bucket emoji (⚔️🛠🏆📚⚠️) so the member sees confirmation
When a member uses /optout <url>: register the opt-out (persistent — prevents re-capture) and delete any archive entry matching that URL
When a member uses /optout-all: remove every archive entry associated with the member's hashed ID
Maintain atlas/capture-log.jsonl with hashed member IDs (never raw)
Honor the guard layer — silently ignore events from strangers in DMs or foreign groups
scope_excludes: Capturing messages without URLs (text-only messages are ignored)
Capturing messages from the bot itself (no echo loop)
Quoting member usernames anywhere in the archive or downstream output
Posting textual messages into the group on URL capture (the reaction is the only outbound surface)
Capturing URLs in DM (DM URL-sharing has no archive context)
Bulk import — only real-time event-driven capture
identity.bot_interaction_pattern: Event-driven via AGENTS.md guidance. The bot's Telegram skill surfaces incoming group messages + slash commands; AGENTS.md tells the bot when to invoke scripts/atlas_capture.py. The guard layer in atlas_lib enforces the trust boundary so strangers can't trigger captures.
identity.user: Members of the configured Telegram group, who get visible confirmation their links are filed.

observable_outcomes: Within 30 seconds of a member posting a URL, the bot reacts with one of the five bucket emojis (or ♻️ for duplicate)
An archive entry appears under archive/{bucket}/ with captured_by = 'app_atlas_article_capture'
archive/index.json gains a new entry; member_id_hash field is a 16-char hex (never the raw user_id)
/optout <url> deletes the matching archive entry and emits CAPTURE_OPT_OUT_REGISTERED
Duplicate URLs (already archived) emit CAPTURE_DUPLICATE and do not double-file
failure_signals: CAPTURE_FAILED:<reason> — fetch, classifier, or write error
CAPTURE_SKIPPED:<reason> — guard refused (stranger DM, foreign group), or classifier returned 'skip'
Member posts URL but no emoji reaction appears within 60s — Telegram plugin or AGENTS.md guidance broken

quality_bar.minimum: Every URL from a verified group member results in either an archive entry + emoji reaction, or a CAPTURE_SKIPPED with a logged reason
quality_bar.excellent: Classification matches the member's mental model; opt-out is never something a member has to do twice for the same link; stranger attempts are silently and reliably refused

privacy: Member identities stored only as salted SHA-256 hashes (first 16 hex chars); raw usernames or user_ids NEVER written to disk anywhere downstream
Article summaries derived from the article body only — never include surrounding chat context
/optout commands MUST delete archive entries unconditionally (no soft-delete, no flag)
Opt-out registry consulted on every capture attempt
safety: Article fetches honor robots.txt; 10s timeout; 5MB max body; UTF-8 best-effort decode
No external posting on member-shared sites (read-only fetch)
Classifier uses tier3 LLM (Haiku); per-call cost capped at $0.005
Malformed classifier output → item logged + skipped, never coerced into a bucket
dependencies: telegram (required) — for group messages, slash commands, reactions
atlas_lib/* (via p-7b26ba5e) — classifier, fetchers, archive, hashing, guard, telegram_api
atlas/operator.json (required by guard.py for membership verification)
atlas/.capture-salt (shared with p-ec644a2a for member-ID hashing)
boundaries: One archive entry per URL — first capture wins on dedup
Reactions on the original member message only — never posts new messages into the group
Operator's BotFather privacy mode MUST be disabled — without it, the bot only sees @-mentions and capture cannot function

user_data_collected: URLs shared in the configured group — fetched, summarized, classified; archived under archive/ until removed via /optout or /optout-all
Telegram user_id of the URL sharer — stored only as a salted SHA-256 hash (first 16 hex chars; salt at atlas/.capture-salt, generated via secrets.token_urlsafe(32) on first capture, never logged)
Telegram message_id of the source message — raw (no message content)
Classification cost per item — raw, local audit telemetry
privacy.opt_out_command: /optout <url> (single item; /optout-all removes every item matching your member hash and registers it to prevent re-capture)
privacy.consent_notice: Atlas archives links shared in this group: the URL, a short summary, and a salted hash of who shared it — never message text. Described in the pinned intro message (installed by atlas-daily-digest). Opt out anytime with /optout <url> or /optout-all.

approved_surfaces: telegram_supergroup:primary_group (react + process shared URLs; membership verified via getChatMember, cached 300s; chat ids in atlas/operator.json)

bot_guidance.content:
**Triggers:** (a) a group message containing one or more URLs, OR (b) an `/optout <URL>` or `/optout-all` slash command in either group or DM.

When you receive a group message containing one or more URLs:

For **each URL**:
1. Write a JSON file at `/tmp/atlas-capture-<msg.id>-<idx>.json` (use a zero-based index per URL in the same message) containing:
   ```
   {"mode": "process",
    "url": "<URL>",
    "message_id": "<msg.id>",
    "member_id": "<from.id>",
    "chat_id": "<chat.id>",
    "chat_type": "<chat.type>"}
   ```
2. Run: `python3 scripts/atlas_capture.py /tmp/atlas-capture-<msg.id>-<idx>.json`
   (no flags — OpenClaw exec preflight blocks complex invocations per `openclaw#87371`.)
3. The script reads the JSON, deletes it, and prints one of:
   - `CAPTURE_ARCHIVED:<bucket>` → react in-thread with bucket emoji: ⚔️ competitive_landscape, 🛠 new_tools, 🏆 use_cases, 📚 case_studies, ⚠️ warnings
   - `CAPTURE_DUPLICATE` → react with ♻️
   - `CAPTURE_OPTED_OUT` or `CAPTURE_FAILED:*` or `CAPTURE_SKIPPED:*` → do nothing visible (logs capture the reason)
4. Do not post a text message in response. The reaction is the only outbound surface.

When you receive an `/optout <URL>` slash command, write `/tmp/atlas-capture-<msg.id>.json` with `{"mode": "opt-out", "url": "<URL>", "member_id": "<from.id>", "chat_id": "<chat.id>", "chat_type": "<chat.type>"}` and run the same script with that path. React with ✅. Do not post a count publicly (privacy).

When you receive an `/optout-all` slash command, write the JSON with `{"mode": "opt-out-all", "member_id": "<from.id>", "chat_id": "<chat.id>", "chat_type": "<chat.type>"}` and run the script. React with ✅. Do not post a count publicly.

**Capture is group-only.** If a URL arrives in a DM, do not invoke atlas_capture — there's no archive context.

Do NOT freelance: if the script invocation fails, do nothing visible. Silence is the documented behavior for any capture failure.

purposes.name: 5-bucket classifier (shared with daily-digest)
purposes.intent: classify item into one of 5 buckets or 'skip'; JSON-only output
purposes.notes: Capture frequency varies by group activity. The bot's daily_cap_usd is the authoritative protection against accidental flood.

recursive_llm.fallback_strategy: If the bot gateway is unreachable, emit CAPTURE_FAILED:classifier_unreachable and DO NOT react. Member will see the message wasn't filed; they can retry by re-sharing the URL later.

files.purpose: Main CLI: process | opt-out | opt-out-all | stats.
Append-only audit log of every capture attempt. Hashed member IDs only.
Persistent opt-out registry. Consulted before every capture.
Salt for member-ID hashing. Generated fresh on first use; never logged; 0600 perms. Recipient generates their own on import — does not travel.

build_spec:
# Atlas Article Capture — Blueprint

## Overview

Event-driven companion to atlas-daily-digest. The bot's Telegram skill surfaces incoming group messages and slash commands; AGENTS.md guidance instructs the bot to invoke `scripts/atlas_capture.py`. The script processes URLs into the shared archive (writing through `atlas_lib.archive`) and handles /optout. Uses the guard from atlas_lib to refuse stranger DMs and foreign groups internally as defense-in-depth.

This app does NOT own atlas_lib — it depends on p-7b26ba5e for the shared modules. All imports come from there.

## File layout

```
scripts/
  atlas_capture.py           ← main CLI: process | opt-out | opt-out-all | stats
atlas/
  capture-log.jsonl          ← created on first capture
  optout.json                ← created on first opt-out
  .capture-salt              ← created on first capture (0600)
```

No cron, no plist — entirely event-driven via AGENTS.md guidance.

## Per-file specs

### scripts/atlas_capture.py
- **Purpose:** Main CLI. Subcommands: `process` (URL → archive), `opt-out` (delete + register opt-out), `opt-out-all` (delete all entries for hashed member), `stats` (last-N-days summary).
- **Inputs:** flags `--url`, `--message-id`, `--member-id`, `--chat-id`, `--chat-type`, `--bot-id`, `--days` (stats only).
- **Guard FIRST (defense-in-depth):** at the top of every subcommand, call `atlas_lib.guard.classify(member_id, chat_id, chat_type, bot_id=bot_id)`. For `process`, refuse anything that's not `(approved_group, member|operator)`. For `opt-out`/`opt-out-all`, allow `approved_group` or `(dm, operator|member)`.
- **process pipeline:** guard check → opt-out check (atlas/optout.json) → duplicate check (atlas_lib.archive.find_duplicate) → fetch URL (atlas_lib.fetchers.fetch_url) → extract summary (HTML tag stripping; first ~800 chars) → classify (atlas_lib.classifier.classify) → if skip → CAPTURE_SKIPPED; if classified → write to archive (atlas_lib.archive.write_item) → emit CAPTURE_ARCHIVED:<bucket>.
- **opt-out pipeline:** guard check → register in atlas/optout.json (atomic write) → atlas_lib.archive.delete_by_url → emit CAPTURE_OPT_OUT_REGISTERED <url> <count>.
- **opt-out-all pipeline:** guard check → atlas_lib.archive.delete_by_member(hash) → emit CAPTURE_OPT_OUT_ALL_REGISTERED <member_hash> <count>.
- **Logging:** every call appends to atlas/capture-log.jsonl with hashed member_id. Best-effort: if workspace doesn't exist (smoke tests), log to stderr and skip the file write.
- **First-run safety:** if optout.json or capture-log.jsonl don't exist, treat as empty.

## Integration with atlas-daily-digest

All the heavy lifting lives in `atlas_lib/*` which p-7b26ba5e owns. This app **imports** from those modules — never redefines them. Key imports:

- `from atlas_lib import guard, hashing` — trust boundary + ID hashing
- `from atlas_lib import classifier as clf` — 5-bucket classifier (name-collision with guard.classify; alias on import)
- `from atlas_lib import archive as arch` — atomic archive read/write
- `from atlas_lib import fetchers, config` — URL fetch + config

If any import fails at runtime (atlas_lib not yet installed because p-7b26ba5e isn't deployed), exit non-zero with a clear error referencing the missing dependency.

The `archive/` directory and `archive/index.json` are SHARED state with p-7b26ba5e. Atlas-daily-digest writes via the same atlas_lib.archive.write_item — atomic writes prevent corruption under concurrent access.

## Recursive LLM concerns

Classifier routes through `atlas_lib.oc_dispatch` (shared with digest; `openclaw_headless` transport). Per recursive_llm contract: exponential backoff max 3, on permanent failure → atlas_lib.classifier returns `bucket: 'skip'`. atlas_capture treats `skip` differently here than digest does: digest skips the item silently, but capture should emit `CAPTURE_FAILED:classifier_unreachable` so the bot KNOWS not to react (and member knows their link wasn't filed by absence of reaction).

## Guard layer details

The guard in atlas_lib.guard runs on every CLI invocation. It needs atlas/operator.json (declared as a file owned by p-7b26ba5e but required by capture too). Without operator.json, ALL events return `(foreign_group, stranger)` and capture refuses everything — that's the safe default, but it means the operator MUST configure operator.json before this app does anything useful.

Membership verification uses Telegram's getChatMember; results cached in atlas/.membership-cache.json (created on first DM from each member) for 5 minutes per (user, chat) pair.

## Test surface

Validate:
- `atlas_capture.py process` against a stranger DM returns `CAPTURE_SKIPPED:not_in_approved_group` (guard works).
- `atlas_capture.py process` against an approved group member with a known URL returns `CAPTURE_ARCHIVED:<bucket>`.
- Re-running same URL same day returns `CAPTURE_DUPLICATE`.
- `atlas_capture.py opt-out --url <url> --member-id <id>` removes the archive entry.
- Raw member IDs never appear in capture-log.jsonl (privacy invariant).

The `test_command` is a fast offline compile + help + stats-empty check; behavioral tests are in `test_cases`.

## What NOT to include

- No new shared modules — depend on p-7b26ba5e's atlas_lib only.
- No cron, no LaunchDaemon, no scheduled execution — entirely event-driven.
- No backfill / bulk-import — only real-time event processing.
- No textual reply messages (the reaction is the only outbound surface).
- No reaction-event handling — OC's Telegram plugin doesn't currently route reactions to bot sessions, so 🤐 reaction-based opt-out is deferred. Use slash commands.
